page: Amazon Web Services c7a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AMD EPYC 9R14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core), the system delivers non-virtualized direct hardware access. It features 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server does not contain integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage infrastructure supported by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier compute and high-throughput memory performance across heavily parallelized tasks. The 192 dedicated cores place the server in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (593,102.61) and PassMark CPU overall score (144,146.68), with notable strength in extended instructions (301,225.18) and encryption tests (238,030.38) utilizing hardware AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. High uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 701.9 GB/sec facilitates top-tier Clang software compilation scores (75,662.0) and ray tracing (170,221.0) under Geekbench suites. Redis SET operations exceed 327 million operations per second, complemented by static web serving throughput of 111.83 GB/sec.

On specialized computing loads such as CPU-based LLM inference, the platform delivers top-tier prompt processing throughput across small (4,593.12 tokens/sec on 135M), medium (343.47 tokens/sec on 7B), and large (44.1 tokens/sec on 70B) architectures via AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 support. However, text generation performance sits within average to strong percentiles due to autoregressive memory-latency bottlenecks typical of CPU inference. From a resource efficiency standpoint, the c7a.metal-48xl maximizes multi-threaded CPU output per socket, though configurations requiring heavy persistent I/O must account for external storage architectural dependencies due to the absence of bundled local NVMe disks.

This hardware footprint matches demanding workloads requiring massive parallel compute density and high DDR5 throughput without hypervisor overhead. Representative deployments include distributed continuous integration and large-scale compilation pipelines, high-density scientific simulation, media rendering, financial physics modeling, and dedicated web-scale caching nodes.

Equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, it supplies a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes no GPUs and relies on network-attached storage over a 50 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks place the server in the top 10% for multi-core compute in stress-ng and PassMark, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 701.9 GB/sec. Without local disks, the system is tuned for large-scale software builds, batch physics simulations, ray tracing, and compute-bound processing clusters.
